senses: Any of several types of public meeting in a Botswana village, especially one involving a gathering of tribal elders.
The place where such a meeting is held.
examples: Speaking at the Mochudi main kgotla after the graduation of at least 1 281 initiates, Kgafela said though there were few challenges, the exercise had been successful.

senses: Not capable of being improved.
A scientist specialising in bryology.
Full of or marked with freckles; sprinkled with spots; freckled.
A longitudinal ridge or projection like the keel of a boat.
ety: Borrowed from Latin carīna (“keel”). Doublet of careen and carene.

senses: A print made by creating the design using oil paint or printer's ink on metal or glass, then transferring the image directly to paper.
The technique of making such prints.
A keyboard-operated typesetting and casting machine that makes and sets separate characters.
ety: From mono- + type or mono- + -type. The printing technique is so called because it allows only one impression to be taken.

senses: Synonym of zoonosis.
A silver coin and unit of currency of various Italian states from the 16th to the 19th centuries.
A former unit of currency in Malta, now the official currency of the Sovereign Military Order of Malta.
A unit of currency in 19th-century Bolivia, equal to 16 soles.
ety: Borrowed from Italian scudo (“a crown, a dollar, a shield”), from Latin scutum (“a shield”). Compare the doublets scute, escudo, scutum, and écu.
examples: And this was the salvation of his house, for several large chunks of plaster cracked off and inside he discovered a pot full of golden scudos.

senses: Smart, clever.
Away from a main location; in a place not owned by a particular organisation.
In any framed work, a horizontal tie other than sill and plate or other principal ties, securing uprights to one another.
A bond or support.
An aromatic glue-like substance produced by honeybees from tree resin, waxes, and their own secretions, used in the construction of their hives.
ety: From Latin propolis, from Hellenistic Ancient Greek πρόπολις (própolis, “suburb; propolis”) (apparently because the material was used by bees to extend their hives), from Ancient Greek προ- (pro-, “pro-”) + πόλις (pólis, “city”).

senses: Pretentious; posturing.
Characterized by social withdrawal and emotional coldness or flattened affectivity.
ety: From schiz(ophrenia)- + -oid, from German, from Ancient Greek σχίζω (skhízō, “to split”) and εἶδος (eîdos, “form, likeness”).

senses: To describe in terms of parameters.
Something boring or dull.
ety: From French soporifique, from Latin sopor (“deep sleep”). Unrelated to stupor (distinct in Proto-Indo-European).

senses: Sportive; lively; joyful.
ety: From game + -ly; compare Old English gamenlīċ (“belonging to games, sportive, theatrical, ridiculous”) and Middle High German gāmelich, gemelich (“joyful”).
examples: That's what I wanted: a challenging race, a gamely fight.
This confirmed the penetration of the theoretical knowledge of color when it is taught using a gamely practice where the act of working come to be a pleasure.
Here was a sober young Harlemite in a gamely tilted bowler with a little French mustache.

senses: A South American ruminant (Lama guanicoe), closely related to the other lamoids, the alpaca, llama, and vicuña in the family Camelidae.
ety: Borrowed from Spanish guanaco, from Quechua wanaku.

senses: One who intrigues; one who forms plots, or pursues an object by secret means.
Synonym of sphenoid.
One who has, or tends to have, original ideas.
One who aims to discover how the writers of a document intended it to be interpreted, and to interpret it in that way.
Specifically, one who aims to discover how the writers of the Constitution of the United States intended it to be interpreted, and to interpret it in that way.
examples: His language is natural and happily wedded to his vivifying conceptions; and last but not least, he is quite unaffected and far above attempts at imitation, that is, he is a true originalist.
So even if drafters' concrete intentions or meta-intentions are closer to the notion of state consent, the originalist is wrong to assume that this notion underpins human rights treaties.
In any event, this professorial detonation, especially coming as it does from hardline Federalist Society constitutional originalists, has set the cat among the Republican pigeons.

senses: One who makes a tapping noise.
A tap-dancer.
A wiretapper.
A beginner; one in the rudiments.
One who is on the point of taking a Master of Arts degree at an English university.
A type of cornbread originating from the northern Andes and resembling a tortilla.
A form of aerobic exercise based on jazz dance.
ety: Blend of jazz + exercise, a trademark of the 1960s.
examples: I don't know when the hearse is gonna be ready, and Mama has her Jazzercise on Mondays.
Denise reports that one of the members of her Jazzercise class works for City Hospital, where the nurses also are organized.

senses: An advocate of intentionalism.
A type of shop or stall in Ancient Rome.
ety: From Latin taberna. Doublet of tavern and taverna.

senses: A stable emulsion that is clear because the individual droplets of the dispersed phase are less than 100 nanometers in diameter
A mechanical piano which uses a roll of perforated paper to operate its keys, instead of being played by a pianist.
A hand that is easy to play, i.e. one that "plays itself".
A miniature parrot of the New World of the genera Forpus, Nannopsittaca and Touit.
One who flubs; a goof, a person who makes errors while speaking.
One who or that which defines something, or provides a definition.
Somewhat happy.
The transformation of an item or creature into something different by magic.
The crescent moon, used in determining the start and end of Islamic months in the Hijri calendar.
A modernist, especially a militantly devoted supporter of modernism
Having the shape of a conoid; having a roughly conical shape.
examples: And a moment later a conoidal bullet struck him square in the chest and knocked him flat in the dirt among his comrades.
Many different forms have been given to the heads of projectiles, as flat, ogival, hemispherical, conoidal, parabolic, blunt trifaced, etc.

senses: One who works for a railroad company.
One who railroads people.
To jointly pay with another or others.
Synonym of string trimmer (“a powered, hand-held garden implement that uses a rotating monofilament line to cut grass, etc., without damaging other objects”).
ety: Blend of string + trimmer, originally a trademark in the United Kingdom.
